release: MAJOR: the tool now tells you when it could not see the site, and refuses to score what it did not read. Measured on an origin that answers 403 to every path — a WAF or an IP allowlist, which is what this scanner meets in the field: the old build reported NEEDS ATTENTION, 50%, QUALITY 71 with zero pages actually read, 87 of 97 rules never evaluated, the words blocked and unreachable appearing nowhere in the report, and the cross-browser section scoring the 403 page itself (two engines agreeing about a block page is not a compatibility result). Now: the report opens with a diagnosis that names the cause — blocked, DNS, route/timeout, connection refused, TLS handshake, server error, 404 entry, redirect dead-end, or non-HTML — each with what to do about it, plus the evidence it was derived from. The verdict is COULD NOT AUDIT, the score and quality are null rather than a number, launch readiness is not ready, and the cross-browser pass does not run on an unreadable origin. It also recognises STATUS PAGES SERVED WITH A 200 (WAF and CDN block pages, Cloudflare interstitials): if every page fetched looks like one the report says the findings may describe an error page, and a real article about HTTP errors is deliberately not flagged. This is a comparability break by design: a result that used to be a number can now be null, which is why the major version moves. A healthy site is unaffected — verified byte-for-byte on a live run. Also in this release: the SEO report renders again (its data island was broken by embedding every audited page raw HTML, so the first </script> in it ended the tag — the payload is escaped now and page source is no longer shipped, 31.6 MB per sgen.com run written twice), a passing check no longer reads NOT RUN (8 of them did on sgen.com, because a clean row carried no identity), a Content and readability section, the SEO checks and page ceiling moved into the Settings gear like every other tool, and an update now applies itself instead of asking you to restart the app.
